newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW-Malaysia Q1 economic growth 8.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Malaysia Q1 economic growth 8.2 pct.

text.p: Following are reactions to Bank Negara's announcement that Malaysia's economic growth in the first quarter of 1997 was 8.2 percent against 8.3 percent in the same period in 1996. Manufacturing growth was 12.9 percent against 14 percent in the comparable periods.
STEPHEN WELLER, DIRECTOR OF STRATEGY, PESAKA JARDINE FLEMING
"It is a comforting thought that the economy is moving along at around 8 percent as opposed to nine percent, which means that the soft landing has been achieved.

The manufacturing growth is more likely to dictate interest rate movement in the near term. It is showing good growth, but it is down about one percent. This leaves room for an interest rate cut in the second half of this year.
"The GDP growth of eight percent means that earnings growth this year is going to be good.
"The figures mean the doom merchants are wrong and they should not tar Malaysia with the same brush as other economies in the region."
"First quarter GDP came in at the high end of expectations. This continues to support scenario that economy is consolidating at around 8.0 percent level.
"Bank Negara Malaysia's 1997 year-end forecast is 8.0 percent.
"In general, the figure suggest that Bank Negara Malaysia will maintain present monetary policy."
KEVIN CHEW, ECONOMIST AT CASPIAN SECURITIES

"The economy is growing at around eight percent as opposed to 9.5 percent in the past, and the trade deficit has improved significantly. So looked at from that angle, we have achieved the soft landing.

"Bank Negara will want to keep monetary policy stable. The factor influencing interest rates this year will be the trade deficit. If it stays at around 13.5 billion, there will be no room for any rate cut. I think Bank Negara will keep monetary policy on hold.
"On the manufacturing side, compared to Singapore it is a very good set of numbers. It is still in double digits".
